title: Air Force Roswell reports: Project Mogul and crash dummies

tellings.quote: Two different reports. So there was the 94 report and then the 96 report. The 94 report was about Project Mosul.
In the 90s in the two 1990 reports they said yes we made this up because it was the coal. We didn't want the Russians to know we were launching these high altitude spy balloons.
tellings.difference: Adds the motive that the cover story kept the Soviets from learning about the high-altitude spy balloons.
tellings.link_reason: The same 1990s Air Force reports that explained Roswell as Project Mogul and crash dummies, told by the same teller.

as_told.title: 1990s Air Force reports on Project Mogul and crash dummies

related.note: Both concern the Air Force's Project Mogul and crash-dummy explanations for Roswell. Shermer presents the 1994 and 1996 reports as the explanation, while the story's teller rejects those explanations.

plain: In the 1990s the US Air Force put out two reports on Roswell, the 1947 incident in which wreckage found near Roswell, New Mexico, was first announced as a flying saucer. A researcher named Michael Shermer, who tells Michels about them from memory without citing the texts, says the 1994 report tied the wreckage to Project Mogul, a secret programme of high-altitude balloons, and a 1996 report followed it. Shermer adds a motive: in his telling the Air Force admitted it had used a cover story because it did not want the Russians to learn it was flying these spy balloons, which would mean the saucer tale grew out of a secret kept for Cold War reasons.
